nodes.question: Despite what trend reported by the National Ministry of Environment and Energy, does Athens still experience air quality issues?
nodes.answer: Athens still experiences air quality issues despite the decreasing trends in air pollution reported by the National Ministry of Environment and Energy over the last two decades.
nodes.paragraph: 2022a, b). Given the limited spatial representation of in situ monitoring stations, atmospheric numerical models, with the support of Earth Observation platforms, can effectively provide support for the prioritization of urban areas neces- sitating compensation actions. The Athens urban area is still subjected to frequent exceedances of the EU air qual- ity standards and the WHO recommendations, despite the decreasing trends reported by the National Ministry of Envi- ronment and Energy during the last two decades (MEEN 2022). The dry, warm and sunny climate, especially in the summer months, promotes the formation of secondary air pollutants through photochemical reactions and the accu- mulation of air pollution in the atmosphere. Moreover, the steadily rising temperatures projected to afflict the Medi- terranean region may lead to increased vulnerability of the local population to air pollution, since high temperatures have been linked to enhanced formation of air pollutants (Petrou et al. 2024). Indeed, during the aforementioned heat- waves of 2021 and 2023 in Athens, city-center PM2.5 con- centration levels were enhanced by 30 and 10%, respectively, compared to the respective average summer value (PM2.5 concentrations retrieved from PANACEA-RI, https:// air- quali ty.
